rules.canonical_statement: Alle Änderungen an diesem Dokument (PROMPTMASTER_GOVERNANCE_V1.md) sind evidence-pflichtig.

rules.title: Rulebook check before any agent action
rules.canonical_statement: No agent executes any action without checking the applicable rulebook first. Rulebooks have priority over individual heuristics.

rules.title: DOS GATES 17 mandatory pre-task gates
rules.canonical_statement: Every agent must pass all 17 DOS GATES (G01-G17) before starting any task: task understanding, goal definition, context check, skill selection, resource check, risk analysis, dependency check, quality criteria, security check, evidence plan, memory sync, audit preparation, policy gate check, time frame, abort criteria, communication plan, final release. Skipping gates requires documented exception.

rules.title: Definition of Done five dimensions
rules.canonical_statement: Every completed work object (task, PR, issue) must satisfy five DoD dimensions: technical (code compiles, tests >=90% coverage, linting clean, no known CVEs, docs updated), functional (all requirements met, acceptance criteria green, edge cases handled, user story complete), design (architecture respected, patterns followed, no duplication, SOLID principles), tracking (kanban updated, task status set, time logged, changelog entry present), governance (audit passed, evidence written, memory synced, rulebooks not violated).

rules.title: Operational Constitution no data loss
rules.canonical_statement: No data loss is permitted. Every transaction must be persisted before a new transaction begins.

rules.title: Security before convenience
rules.canonical_statement: Security is non-negotiable and takes precedence over convenience in all decisions and implementations.

rules.title: State reproducibility from logs and evidence
rules.canonical_statement: Every system state must be reconstructable from logs and evidence. Full audit trail is required.

rules.title: Decision transparency
rules.canonical_statement: All decisions must be documented in a traceable, comprehensible manner.

rules.title: Automation first principle
rules.canonical_statement: Manual steps are errors. Automate everything possible.

rules.title: CI/CD pipeline mandatory stages
rules.canonical_statement: Every commit must pass through lint, test, build, security scan, and audit stages. Pipeline failure blocks deployment and triggers immediate notification.

rules.title: Rollback within five minutes
rules.canonical_statement: Rollbacks must be possible and executable within 5 minutes of detection.

rules.title: Confidence model three levels
rules.canonical_statement: High confidence (all checks green, tests >90%, audit passed) enables automatic deployment. Medium confidence (minor deviations, <90% coverage) requires manual approval. Low confidence (critical errors, security issues) blocks deployment and triggers immediate escalation.

rules.title: Brain-first before every decision
rules.canonical_statement: The Brain must be consulted before every decision. The Brain contains architecture, patterns, decision logs, and context. Without Brain access, tasks must pause and must not guess.

rules.title: Skill-first loading mandate
rules.canonical_statement: Skills are the only source for executable capabilities. No agent improvises capabilities that exist as skills. Skills must be loaded before work begins.

rules.title: Memory duty central memory layer
rules.canonical_statement: agentmemory is the central memory layer. No agent-local memory is permitted outside agentmemory. Every relevant interaction must be stored in agentmemory.

rules.title: Do not guess when uncertain
rules.canonical_statement: When uncertain, agents must ask or pause the task. Guessing is not permitted.

rules.title: No data deletion without confirmation
rules.canonical_statement: No data may be removed without explicit confirmation.

rules.title: Evidence required for every action
rules.canonical_statement: Every action produces evidence. Evidence capture is mandatory.

rules.title: No side effects outside defined scope
rules.canonical_statement: Actions may only execute within their defined scope. Side effects beyond the defined scope are prohibited.

rules.title: Rule hierarchy for conflict resolution
rules.canonical_statement: Rule hierarchy from highest to lowest priority: Operational Constitution (1), GLOBAL_POLICY_V1 (2), NeXify AI Global Rules (3), MEMORY_PFLICHT_V1 (4), DOS GATES (5), DOS Definition of Done (6), DONE_REGEL_V1 (7), SKILL_FIRST_REGEL_V1 (8), AUDIT_MASTER_V1 (9), EVIDENCE_TEMPLATE_V1 (10), FEEDBACK_LOOP_MASTER_V1 (11), RULE_CONFLICT_REGISTER (12), BRAIN_GEBOT_V1 and BRAIN_BEGRIFF_DEFINITION_V1 (13), POSITIVE_SURPRISE_DELIVERY_RULE_V1 (14), GOOSE.md and GOOSE_NEXIFY_AUTOMATION_RULES (15).

rules.title: Conflict resolution higher rank or more specific
rules.canonical_statement: When two rulebooks directly contradict, the higher-ranked entry decides. At equal rank, the more specific rulebook decides. Unsolvable conflicts must be documented in the RULE_CONFLICT_REGISTER.

rules.title: Index changes require evidence
rules.canonical_statement: All changes to this rulebook index are evidence-mandatory.

rules.title: Index is single source of truth for rulebooks
rules.canonical_statement: This index catalogs all active rulebooks in the NeXify system, summarizes core rules from existing sources, documents new regulations, and serves as the single source of truth for the rulebook landscape.

rules.title: Conflict register audit obligation
rules.canonical_statement: This rule conflict register requires mandatory audit. Every active conflict must be regularly reviewed according to defined monitoring intervals.

rules.title: Conflict register captures all known rule conflicts
rules.canonical_statement: This register serves as the central decision basis for rule conflicts. It documents all known conflicts, contradictions, and tensions between active rule works in the NeXify system. Goal is transparency about rule inconsistencies and systematic resolution.

rules.title: Conflict classification with mandatory handling
rules.canonical_statement: Every conflict is classified as BREAKING (system block, immediate escalation and rule adaptation required), MAJOR (hindering, resolve in next iteration), MINOR (known inconsistency, observe and check at next revision), or RESOLVED (fixed, document solution).

rules.title: Conflict closure only on resolution or explicit acceptance
rules.canonical_statement: A conflict is only closed when resolved or explicitly accepted. Until then it remains open and must be tracked in the register.

rules.title: Every agent must report new rule conflicts
rules.canonical_statement: A conflict not in the register does not exist. Every agent is obligated to report new conflicts using the defined template format, which includes status, affected rules, conflict description, impact, and resolution approach.

rules.title: Conflict monitoring schedule by severity
rules.canonical_statement: On rule work update: check all conflicts for currency. Weekly: review MINOR conflicts. Monthly: prioritize MAJOR conflict resolution. On BREAKING: immediate action and escalation.

rules.title: K001: Skill-First vs. Exploration blocks novel tasks
rules.canonical_statement: SKILL_FIRST_REGEL_V1 and the 'Nicht raten' rule together prohibit action without a prepared skill. This suppresses exploration and creativity for tasks that have no existing skill. Mitigation: create an exploration skill or add an exploration exception to GLOBAL_POLICY_V1. Status: MAJOR unresolved.

rules.title: K002: DONE completeness vs. time-box constraint
rules.canonical_statement: DONE_REGEL_V1 requires 6 completion criteria (goal, tests, evidence, memory, kanban, audit). DOS GATES G14 defines a time budget. Complex tasks may exceed time budget when fulfilling full DONE checks. Mitigation: separate time budget for DONE check or define DONE as its own task. Status: MAJOR unresolved.

rules.title: K003: Policy gate overhead on simple tasks
rules.canonical_statement: GLOBAL_POLICY_V1 requires 5-stage gates for every action. For simple actions (file read, status check) this overhead is disproportionate. Quick-check shortcut defined in GLOBAL_POLICY_V1 section 3 exists but needs integration into skills. Status: MINOR unresolved.

rules.title: K004: Audit requirement vs.feedback loops may cause infinite cycles
rules.canonical_statement: DONE_REGEL_V1 requires a passed audit before completion. Feedback loops may trigger changes requiring re-audit, potentially creating an infinite cycle. Mitigation: define maximum 2 audit cycles per task, escalate to human after 2nd cycle. Status: MINOR unresolved.

rules.title: K005: Memory requirement vs.agent isolation on agentmemory failure
rules.canonical_statement: MEMORY_PFLICHT_V1 requires central memory. Prime Directive 1 requires persistence before new transactions. If agentmemory fails, PD1 blocks new transactions but recovery without memory is hard. Mitigation: local read-only cache fallback and separate recovery process. Status: MINOR unresolved.

rules.title: Conflict register changelog version tracking
rules.canonical_statement: All changes to this conflict register must be documented in the changelog with date, version, change description, and author.

rules.title: Skill-First Mandate — Load skill before any work
rules.canonical_statement: Before any work, agents MUST check if a skill exists for the task, load it fully into context, confirm the documentation is read and understood, then execute work using the loaded skill. No action without loaded skill.

rules.title: No improvisation of existing or missing skills
rules.canonical_statement: Skills are the only authorized source for executable capabilities. No agent may improvise capabilities that exist or should exist as a skill. If no skill exists, pause work and request skill creation.

rules.title: Skill definition and storage requirements
rules.canonical_statement: A valid skill must be stored in /workspace/nexify/05_skills/, have a clear description, a defined input/output schema, a version number, and be tested and auditable.

rules.title: Skill exists and is loaded — proceed with work
rules.canonical_statement: If a skill exists and is already loaded into context, the agent may proceed to execute work directly.

rules.title: Skill exists but not loaded — load then work
rules.canonical_statement: If a skill exists but is not loaded into context, the agent MUST load the skill first, then execute the work.

rules.title: Skill exists but outdated — update then load then work
rules.canonical_statement: If a skill exists but is outdated, the agent MUST update the skill first, then load it, then execute the work.

rules.title: Skill does not exist — pause work and request creation
rules.canonical_statement: If a skill does not exist for the required task, the agent MUST pause work and request skill creation before proceeding.

rules.title: Skill exists but insufficient — extend then load then work
rules.canonical_statement: If a skill exists but does not fully cover the task, the agent MUST extend the skill first, then load it, then execute the work.

rules.title: Skill is defective — prioritize repair, pause work
rules.canonical_statement: If a skill is defective or faulty, the agent MUST prioritize skill repair and pause all work until the skill is restored.

rules.title: Forbidden: Improvise capability without a skill
rules.canonical_statement: It is forbidden to improvise a capability without a skill. This is risky and not reproducible. The alternative is to create or load the appropriate skill.

rules.title: Forbidden: Bypass skill via prompt injection
rules.canonical_statement: It is forbidden to bypass skill requirements via prompt injection as this circumvents quality gates. Use the Policy Gate instead.

rules.title: Forbidden: Claim skill output as own work
rules.canonical_statement: It is forbidden to present a skill's result as one's own work. This constitutes lack of transparency. Evidence must be documented.

rules.title: Forbidden: Invoke skill without reviewing documentation
rules.canonical_statement: It is forbidden to invoke a skill without prior review of its documentation. This is operating blind. Skill documentation must be read before use.

rules.title: Skill loading pre-work checklist
rules.canonical_statement: Before each work session, agents must verify: (1) relevant skills identified, (2) skill loaded in active context, (3) documentation read, (4) skill tested/valid, (5) skill fully covers the task scope.

rules.title: Skill usage is audit-mandatory
rules.canonical_statement: Skill usage is subject to mandatory audit as referenced by AUDIT_MASTER_V1. All skill invocations must be auditable.

rules.title: Exception for novel tasks with no existing skill
rules.canonical_statement: If a task is novel and no skill yet exists, the agent may start the skill creation process instead of loading a skill. The exception must be documented in the RULE_CONFLICT_REGISTER.

rules.title: Exception for trivial operations like reading files
rules.canonical_statement: Trivial operations such as reading a file or listing a directory do not require a skill. However, evidence documentation remains mandatory even for trivial operations.

rules.title: Skill-First rule hierarchy and relationships
rules.canonical_statement: This rule (Skill-First) operates at Rank 3 in NeXify AI Global Rules. It references GLOBAL_POLICY_V1 (skill check is stage 1 of policy gate), MEMORY_PFLICHT_V1 (skills referenced in agentmemory), DOS GATES G04 (gate 4 = skill selection), and AUDIT_MASTER_V1 (skill usage audit-mandatory).

rules.title: Query Brain before non-trivial work
rules.canonical_statement: Before any non-trivial coding, refactoring, debugging, deployment or review work, the agent must query the NeXify Brain (nexifyai_brain collection) for relevant context, prior decisions and stored knowledge. This applies to all agents (Claude Code, Goose CLI, Goose ACC). Brain-unavailable scenarios allow only safe read-only analysis or stop-and-report.

rules.title: Store durable knowledge after changes
rules.canonical_statement: After completing meaningful changes, decisions or findings, the agent must store durable knowledge in the NeXify Brain (nexifyai_brain collection) using embedding-optimized structure. This includes design decisions, runtime findings, learned rules, configuration changes and problem resolutions. Do not store raw secrets.

rules.title: No systemmaster work with untested Brain
rules.canonical_statement: The agent must not perform systemmaster-level work (deployment, infrastructure changes, global configuration) if the Brain API is untested or unreachable. Brain connectivity must be verified before such work begins. If Brain is unavailable, only safe read-only analysis or stop-and-report is permitted.

rules.title: Report Brain status in every task completion
rules.canonical_statement: Every task completion report must include Brain status: whether Brain was queried before work, whether knowledge was stored after work, and any Brain connectivity issues encountered. This ensures traceability and enables auditing of Brain-first compliance across all agents.

rules.title: Gate step 1: Submit change proposal with diff for prompt changes
rules.canonical_statement: Aenderungsvorschlag einreichen (mit Diff). Any prompt change must begin with a formal proposal including a diff of the intended modification.

rules.title: Gate step 2: PROMPTMASTER reviews impact on dependent systems
rules.canonical_statement: Promptmaster prueft Auswirkung auf abhaengige Systeme. Every change proposal must undergo a dependency impact analysis by PROMPTMASTER before approval.

rules.title: Gate step 3: Risk assessment classifies change as LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL
rules.canonical_statement: Risikobewertung (LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / CRITICAL). All prompt changes must receive a formal risk classification before proceeding through the gate.

rules.title: Gate step 4: CRITICAL changes require staging test and rollback plan
rules.canonical_statement: Bei CRITICAL: Staging-Test + Rollback-Plan. CRITICAL-risk prompt changes must pass staging tests and have a documented rollback plan before production deployment.

rules.title: Gate step 5: Document evidence of all prompt changes
rules.canonical_statement: Evidence dokumentieren. All prompt change actions and approvals must be documented with evidence references for auditability.

rules.title: Gate step 6: Obtain gate release approval before deploying prompt change
rules.canonical_statement: Gate-Freigabe einholen. Formal approval from the gate authority must be obtained before any prompt change is rolled out to production.

rules.title: Gate step 7: Roll out approved prompt change to production
rules.canonical_statement: Aenderung ausrollen. After gate approval, the prompt change may be deployed to the production environment.

rules.title: Gate step 8: Post-change health check after prompt deployment
rules.canonical_statement: Post-Change Health Check. After every prompt change rollout, a health check must verify system stability and prompt effectiveness.

rules.title: Gate step 9: Update prompt register after change completion
rules.canonical_statement: Register aktualisieren. The prompt verankerung register must be updated to reflect all completed changes, including new status, evidence references, and timestamps.

rules.title: System-Instructions Identity is a protected prompt under PROMPTMASTER
rules.canonical_statement: System-Instructions (Identity) is a protected prompt and may not be modified outside the PROMPTMASTER gate process.

rules.canonical_statement: CLAUDE.md (falls vorhanden) is a protected prompt and may not be modified outside the PROMPTMASTER gate process.

rules.canonical_statement: 9Router-Config-Prompts are protected prompts and may not be modified outside the PROMPTMASTER gate process.

rules.title: No Full Crash Policy applies to all NeXify systems
rules.canonical_statement: NO FULL CRASH POLICY V1 (v1.0.0, rank 3) is BINDING on ALL_NEXIFY_SYSTEMS with CI_GATE_AUTOMATED enforcement. Created 2026-06-11, last reviewed 2026-06-11.

rules.title: Critical protected systems require highest safety measures
rules.canonical_statement: CRITICAL protected systems: 9Router, Brain/Qdrant, agentmemory, Oracle, Cloudflare/Tunnel/DNS, Supabase, Redis/Postgres, Secret-Management. These systems must never experience full outage.

rules.title: High protected systems require strong safety measures
rules.canonical_statement: HIGH protected systems: Hermes WebUI/Workstation, Auto-Chat/User-Chat-Driver, Vercel, Goose ACC, Claude Code Systemmaster, SimpleX Gateway, MCP Server. Partial failure tolerated for these systems.

rules.title: Full backup required before system changes
rules.canonical_statement: Before changes, create full backup of affected system. Required for all operations on protected systems.

rules.title: Export and save current config before changes
rules.canonical_statement: Before changes, export current configuration of affected system and save it securely.

rules.title: Documented rollback plan required
rules.canonical_statement: Before changes, create documented plan for system restoration to known-good state.

rules.title: Capture health metrics baseline before changes
rules.canonical_statement: Before changes, record current health metrics of affected system as baseline for comparison.

rules.title: Detailed change plan with steps required
rules.canonical_statement: Before changes, produce detailed change plan enumerating every step of the operation.

rules.title: Assign risk level before every change
rules.canonical_statement: Every change must be classified as LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL risk before execution.

rules.title: Define and enforce approval procedure per risk
rules.canonical_statement: Each risk level requires specific approval gate: LOW=none, MEDIUM=code_review, HIGH=approval_and_review, CRITICAL=multi_stage_gate_plus_staging.

rules.title: Prepare evidence document before changes
rules.canonical_statement: Before changes, prepare evidence document template to record compliance with policy requirements.

rules.title: Run health check after every change
rules.canonical_statement: After change completion, perform health check on affected system to verify operational state.

rules.title: LOW risk: no outage, documentation only
rules.canonical_statement: LOW risk means no outage risk, documentation only. No approval gate required. Examples: writing evidence, updating README.

rules.title: MEDIUM risk: low outage, degraded ops possible
rules.canonical_statement: MEDIUM risk means low outage probability, degraded operation possible. Gate: code_review. Examples: config changes with rollback, plugin test.

rules.title: HIGH risk: subsystem outage possible
rules.canonical_statement: HIGH risk means outage risk for subsystems. Gate: approval_and_review. Examples: changing 9Router provider, DNS changes.

rules.title: CRITICAL risk: full system outage possible
rules.canonical_statement: CRITICAL risk means full outage risk for entire system. Gate: multi_stage_gate_plus_staging. Examples: 9Router restart, secret rotation, DB migration.

rules.title: No hard restart of 9Router without rollback
rules.canonical_statement: Hard restart of 9Router without documented rollback plan is forbidden.

rules.title: No config overwrite without backup
rules.canonical_statement: Overwriting configuration without prior backup is forbidden.

rules.title: No provider deletion without verification
rules.canonical_statement: Deleting any provider without prior verification and impact check is forbidden.

rules.title: Never remove or overwrite nexifyai-combo-llm
rules.canonical_statement: Removing or overwriting nexifyai-combo-llm model is forbidden.

rules.title: Never write secrets in plaintext to Git/Evidence/Brain/Logs
rules.canonical_statement: Writing secret values in plaintext to Git repositories, evidence documents, Brain, or logs is forbidden.

rules.title: No risky live changes without staging or shadow test
rules.canonical_statement: Riskant live changes without staging environment or shadow test are forbidden.

rules.title: No full crash risk without documented emergency plan
rules.canonical_statement: Risking full system crash without documented emergency/fallback plan is forbidden.

rules.title: No production prompt changes without Promptmaster review
rules.canonical_statement: Changing production prompts without Promptmaster review is forbidden.

rules.title: No DNS or tunnel changes without rollback plan
rules.canonical_statement: Changing DNS records or Cloudflare Tunnel configuration without documented rollback plan is forbidden.

rules.title: No database migration without backup
rules.canonical_statement: Running database migration without prior backup is forbidden.

rules.title: Track policy violations with required fields and ID format
rules.canonical_statement: Violations must be recorded with: violation_id, date, system, category, perpetrator, impact, immediate_action, prevention, evidence_path. ID format: V-{YYYYMMDD}-{NR}.

rules.title: No blocking confirmations for safe internal work
rules.canonical_statement: Safe internal operations must never present blocking confirmation prompts. Non-interactive execution proceeds automatically for approved categories.

rules.title: Gate tasks produce approval packages not terminal prompts
rules.canonical_statement: Gated operations must generate structured approval packages instead of blocking at the terminal. The package contains operation details, impact assessment, and rollback plan.

rules.title: Unknown prompts are captured not blocking
rules.canonical_statement: Unrecognized or unclassified prompts must be captured into a review queue rather than blocking execution. The system logs the unknown prompt context for later classification.

rules.title: Auto-approval matrix governs all tool use
rules.canonical_statement: All tool invocations in non-interactive mode are governed by a predefined auto-approval matrix that classifies operations by risk category and determines approval action.

rules.title: Secrets must never appear in prompts or logs
rules.canonical_statement: API keys, tokens, passwords, and other secrets must be masked or omitted from all prompts, logs, and output to prevent exposure in non-interactive execution traces.

rules.title: Destructive commands require gate and rollback plan
rules.canonical_statement: Commands that modify, delete, or irreversibly alter system state require gated approval with an accompanying rollback or recovery plan before execution.

rules.title: READONLY operations auto-approved
rules.canonical_statement: Read-only operations such as file reads, status checks, and queries are automatically approved without human intervention.

rules.title: SAFE_INTERNAL operations auto-approved
rules.canonical_statement: Internal safe operations including configuration reads and non-destructive admin commands are automatically approved.

rules.title: TEST operations auto-approved
rules.canonical_statement: Test execution operations including running test suites and test helpers are automatically approved.

rules.title: DOCS operations auto-approved
rules.canonical_statement: Documentation operations including reading, writing, and transforming documentation files are automatically approved.

rules.title: GATED operations require approval package
rules.canonical_statement: Gated operations produce structured approval packages containing operation details and impact assessment for human review before execution.

rules.title: SECRET_RISK operations blocked
rules.canonical_statement: Operations that handle or expose secrets are blocked in non-interactive mode. No automatic approval is possible for secret-risk operations.

rules.title: DESTRUCTIVE operations blocked
rules.canonical_statement: Destructive operations that modify, delete, or irreversibly alter system state are blocked in non-interactive mode. Requires human approval with rollback plan.

rules.title: EXTERNAL_WRITE operations require approval package
rules.canonical_statement: Operations that write to external systems or services produce approval packages for human review before execution.

rules.title: UNKNOWN operations captured and held
rules.canonical_statement: Unknown or unclassified operations are captured into a review queue and held for classification rather than being auto-approved, blocked, or proceeding.

rules.title: Positive-Surprise-Delivery-Rule V1
rules.canonical_statement: Agents must deliver positive surprises beyond minimum requirements by adding better structure, evidence, tests, documentation, registers, task decomposition, clear next actions, error prevention, rule/skill/prompt improvements, and quality checks.

rules.title: Erlaubte Verbesserungen (Allowed Improvements)
rules.canonical_statement: Only improvements in these categories are allowed: better structure, additional evidence, better tests, better documentation, missing registers, better task decomposition, clear next actions, error prevention, rule/skill/prompt improvement, brain/agentmemory pending, quality checks.

rules.title: Verbotene Verbesserungen (Forbidden Improvements)
rules.canonical_statement: These improvements are forbidden: scope explosion, risky external changes, customer project changes without gate, facade without function.

rules.title: Entscheidungsmatrix (Decision Matrix)
rules.canonical_statement: Decision flow: goal reached AND safe improvement possible AND in allowed scope THEN execute improvement. All three conditions must be true before proceeding.

rules.title: Auditpflicht (Audit Requirement)
rules.canonical_statement: All positive surprise delivery actions require mandatory audit logging. Every improvement executed under this rule must be auditable.

rules.title: Promptmaster-Rolle mit exklusiven Prompt-Änderungsrechten
rules.canonical_statement: Nur Promptmaster darf produktive Prompts ändern, löschen, deployen und reviewen. Andere Agenten haben ausschließlich Lese-, Erkennungs- und Vorschlagsrechte.

rules.title: Andere Agenten dürfen Prompts nicht eigenmächtig ändern
rules.canonical_statement: Andere Agenten dürfen keine eigenmächtigen Prompt-Änderungen vornehmen, kein CLAUDE.md ohne Review ändern, keine Prompt-Dateien direkt editieren, keine Prompt-Templates überschreiben und keine System-Prompts im Memory überschreiben.

rules.title: Fünfstufiger Change-Control-Prozess für Prompt-Änderungen
rules.canonical_statement: Jede Prompt-Änderung durchläuft fünf Schritte: (1) Erkennen durch jeden Agenten, (2) Vorschlag mit IST/SOLL-Vergleich und Evidence, (3) Review durch Promptmaster, (4) Test in Isolation und Regression, (5) Deploy mit Versionierung und Backup.

rules.title: Vier Dringlichkeitsstufen für Prompt-Probleme
rules.canonical_statement: Prompt-Probleme werden in vier Stufen eingeteilt: P1 (kritisch, Sicherheitslücke/Systemausfall, SLA 1h), P2 (hoch, fehlerhafte Ausgaben/Datenverlust-Risiko, SLA 4h), P3 (normal, Verbesserung/Klarstellung, SLA 48h), P4 (niedrig, Kosmetik/Optimierung, SLA 2 Wochen).

rules.title: CLAUDE.md-Inhalts-Governance mit erlaubten und verbotenen Inhalten
rules.canonical_statement: CLAUDE.md darf nur globale Systemregeln, immer-gültige Workflow-Anweisungen, Sicherheitsrichtlinien, Verhaltenscodizes und Qualitätsstandards enthalten. Verboten sind task-spezifische Anweisungen, temporäre Workarounds, benutzerspezifische Konfigurationen, Debugging-Anweisungen und experimentelle Konfigurationen.

rules.title: CLAUDE.md-Änderungsregeln mit Evidence-Pflicht
rules.canonical_statement: CLAUDE.md-Änderungen dürfen nicht überladen werden, keine task-spezifischen Anweisungen enthalten, brauchen Review vor Commit, haben Evidence-Pflicht und müssen systemweite Gültigkeit begründen.

rules.title: Eskalationsregeln bei nicht erreichbarem Promptmaster
rules.canonical_statement: Wenn Promptmaster nicht erreichbar ist, übernimmt Oracle temporär. Bei abgelehnten Änderungen kann Autor Beschwerde bei Oracle einlegen. Bei kritischen Prompt-Fehlern (P1) wird Promptmaster sofort benachrichtigt. Oracle entscheidet bei Uneinigkeit als letzte Instanz.

rules.title: Prompt-Governance-Qualitätsmetriken mit Zielwerten
rules.canonical_statement: Folgende Metriken gelten: Change-Request-Zykluszeit < 48h (P3), Approval-Rate > 70%, Rollback-Rate < 5%, Prompt-Test-Abdeckung 100%, CLAUDE.md-Änderungsfrequenz < 5 pro Monat.

rules.title: Verbotene Prompt-Aktionen mit Konsequenzen
rules.canonical_statement: Eigenmächtige Prompt-Änderungen führen zu sofortiger Meldung an Oracle, Audit und möglicher Sperrung. CLAUDE.md-Überladung ohne Review wird rückgängig gemacht. Direkte Prompt-Datei-Edits werden rückgängig mit obligatorischem Change-Control. Überschriebene Templates werden aus Backup wiederhergestellt mit Dependency-Check. Überschriebene System-Prompts im Memory werden aus Backup restored mit Oracle-Benachrichtigung.

rules.title: Promptmaster hat volle Schreib-, Änderungs-, Lösch-, Deploy- und Review-Rechte
rules.canonical_statement: Promptmaster besitzt die Berechtigungen: prompt_schreiben, prompt_aendern, prompt_loeschen, prompt_deployen, prompt_review, prompt_testen und claude_md_aendern. Promptmaster trägt Verantwortung für Pflege, Qualitätssicherung, Versionierung, Change-Control und Test vor Produktivsetzung.

rules.title: Andere Agenten haben Erkennungs- und Vorschlagsrechte für Prompts
rules.canonical_statement: Andere Agenten dürfen Fehler in Prompts erkennen und melden, konkrete Änderungsvorschläge mit Evidence einreichen und Verbesserungen vorschlagen statt selbst zu ändern. Tests nur in isolierter Umgebung.

rules.title: Promptmaster-Governance gilt für alle NeXify-Prompts
rules.canonical_statement: Diese Governance gilt für alle Prompts im NeXify-System: 04_prompts/, CLAUDE.md, System-Prompts und Prompt-Templates. Regel-Rang 5.
